territorial_scope.description: Applies to data centers in the State of New Jersey.

evidence.quote: data center in the State shall prepare and submit a water and energy usage

summary.short: Requires owners and operators of New Jersey data centers to submit semi-annual water and energy usage reports to the Board of Public Utilities, which publishes the submitted usage information. Reporting runs for three years from first submission; performance and sustainability data stay confidential. Effective immediately.
summary.long: Requires owners and operators of New Jersey data centers to report water and energy usage to the Board of Public Utilities (BPU), first within six months after the act takes effect (three months for facilities operating a year or more), then semi-annually. Reports cover facility details, energy consumption, the serving electric public utility and its agreements, on-site power, and water input and sources. Data centers receiving a State financial incentive must also report performance and sustainability indicators, which are confidential; others may submit them voluntarily. The Board publishes submitted usage information within 30 days, excluding confidential data. Operators must notify the Board at least 60 days before substantial operational or technology changes. The reporting duty runs for three years from first submission, after which the Board decides whether to continue it and adopts rules under the Administrative Procedure Act if so. Excludes data centers primarily used for internal operations of licensed health care providers, unless operated as commercial colocation. The Board consults the Department of Environmental Protection. The act takes effect immediately.

notes: The fetched text is a bill (Second Reprint of S3379, with the Assembly committee amendments of June 4, 2026), not an enacted session law. The enactment and in-force status come from the registry metadata, not from this text. The text contains reprint markers (^1, ^2, brackets) showing insertions and deletions; the annotation reads the text as shown, including marked insertions. Internal tensions: subsection b. sets a six-month first-report deadline, or three months for facilities operating at least one year, while subsection f. limits the reporting requirement to three years from first submission; subsection c. requires performance and sustainability data only from facilities receiving State financial incentives, and subsection d.(1) bars publication of that data but says aggregated figures from at least five facilities are to be included in the report. The 'Data center' definition carries a marked exclusion for certain health-care facilities. The Department of Environmental Protection is named only as a consultation partner (subsection g.) and is not coded as a relation.
